Id. due to the king by her husband at his death by instalments of 20 marks yearly at the exchequer, payable at Easter and Michaelmas, and although he afterwards revoked the said extension of the time of payment, willing that she should pay 20Z. yearly at the said feasts and granted such 20Z. yearly to Edmund de Ufford in satisfaction of an annuity of 20Z. at the exchequer granted to him for life, until the said debt should be extinguished, he now wills that the first grant of extension shall be of force and that the said assignment of 20Z. yearly to Edmund shall be of none effect, but he. shall have the said 20 marks yearly and 10 marks  June 25. Westminster. June 20. Westminster. Membrane 2—cont. yearly at the exchequer, until the debt of the said sheriff be fully paid, and then he shall have the said 201. yearly at the exchequer again. By p.s.

Inspeximus of letters patent, dated 15 November, 7 Edward I, discharging John Sampson and Roger Basy, citizens of York, of all debts at the Jewry in respect of certain land with schools thereon, whereof queen Eleanor enfeoffed them; and confirmation of the same to Master Thomas Sampson, now tenant of the land. By fine of 4 mark. York. Feb. 11.

Whereas the king by letters patent lately granted for life to Janotus de Ispannia, a convert, such sustenance for life out of the House of Converts, London, as other converts receive there, the said Janotus has made supplication that, inasmuch as there is no mention in the letters patent of how much he is to receive for such sustenance, the king will grant him 10J</. at the exchequer weekly, as the other converts have and Edward le Convers used to receive and the king has granted his request. By p.s.

Grant to Roger de Stretford, chaplain, on testimony before the king Westminster, that he has long served in the office of chaplain in the king's chapel of the Converts of London without certain provision as yet made for his sustenance, of the said office of chaplain for life, receiving yearly by his own hands from the rector of the church of St. Dunstan West, Fletestret, London, those 6 marks which the rector is bound to pay the chaplain serving in the said chapel; and grant also that, when he can no longer discharge the office for bodily weakness, whereby he must find another chaplain in his place, he shall have for life for his sustenance as much out of the rents of the House of Converts and of what the converts receive yearly at the exchequer as one of the converts has, by the hands of the keeper of the said house. By p.s. April 5.

Whereas the prior and brethren of the Hospital of St. John of Jerusalem in England lately of their own free will granted by their letters to Edward de Sancto Johanne, now a convert, because he procured the deliverance of Roger de Stayngrave, a brother of the Hospital, from the prison of the sultan of Babylon (soldani Babilone) and brought him to England, at very great expense to himself, and also at the request of the king's father and for a great sum of money then paid by the said Edward to the prior and brethren, a corrody or sustenance and an annual pension of 20 marks out of their house of Clerkenwell and certain of their lands, and whereas the now prior, fearing that when Edward dies he and his house may suffer damage by the grant of such corrody and pension at the request of the king (reqiam), has prayed the king instantly for an indemnity in this behalf: the king has granted that the prior and brethren and their suc­ cessors shall uot be charged with a like corrody or pension after the death of the said Edward, nor shall the grant of the same to him prejudice their house as a precedent. By p.s.  Membrane 16—cont.

Commission of oyer and terminer to William de Thorpe, Edmund de Grymesby, Nicholas de Bokelond and Robert de Thorpe, touching an information that in the king's forest of Bernewod, co. Buckingham, trespasses of vert and venison as well as purprestures and assarts have been committed before these times, and that the foresters and other ministers of that forest, without just title claiming divers fees therein, by colour of those fees, carry away and convert to their own use issues, profits and emoluments of right pertaining to the king. By C.

Commission of oyer and terminer to William de Shareshull, Roger Hillary, Thomas de Berkele of Coberle and William de Chiltenham, on complaint by Richard Talbot that Alexander de Carent, Richard Irby, Walter de Nasse, John de Pulesdon of Strete, Thomas, his brother, Alexander Hoke, John de Houle, John Sekerwal, Walter Hok, Richard Penyerd, William de Hereford, chaplain, John de Hereford, chaplain, and others broke his close and houses at Ruwardyn, co. Gloucester, and carried away his goods. By K.  Membrane 20'/—rant. are not, extort victuals and large sums not only of false but of good money in the counties of Norfolk, Suffolk and Essex, and convert the same to their own use, and that to be more fully certified of the premises he has appointed the said Hugh, John and Ralph to find by inquisitions the names of the said evildoers and all particulars of their frauds and then to arrest all those indicted by the inquisitions and imprison them until he give further order therein. « By C. MEMBRANE ltW Commission to Simon Basset, sheriff of Gloucester, Walter le Waryner and Robert de Orcheston reciting that, whereas the king because John Pouchet, 'Lumbard,' his enemy, with 100/. of his money delivered to the said John by the hands of Master Bernard de Saltu, king's clerk, to do certain business for the king, lies hid and runs to and fro refusing to satisfy him of the money, by writ directed the said sheriff, to take him and bring him before the council, and the sheriff when the said John should come out of the church of Tettebury in which on that account he kept himself, would have done so, certain evildoers took John by force from the church with the king's money and let him go free, and that the king has appointed them to find by inquisition the names of all those concerned in the taking of him from the church..

Grant, for life, to Theobald de Turkie, a convert to the catholic faith and baptized, who is destitute and cannot help himself from other sources, of such state and sustenance as one of the king's converts dwelling in the city of London has and receives there as in houses for his habitation and wages at the exchequer, rents and other things. By p.s.

Commission to John de Radeclyve, Roger de Normanvylle and John de Alvetham to make inquisition in the county of Lancaster touching an information that wastes and sales have been made by Richard de Norton, parker of the king's park of Ightenhull, and John de Norton, his lieutenant there, as well in the king's manor in that park, as of the vert and venison in the park, that Richard beyond the number of his animals feeding in the park by reason of his office has forty animals feeding there at the king's charges and converts the profit arising from these to his own use, and that he feeds there likewise three mares with the king's stallions, and the issues of the mares with the issues of the king's mares, every year to the king's great damage.

Grant to Agnes daughter of Edward de Sancto Johanne, because her father was a convert and she is of tender age and destitute of the help of friends, that she shall have for life a chamber in the House of Converts, London, and her portion of the rents and other profits and alms pertaining to the said House, as well as such wages as a convert receives of the king's grant at the exchequer. By p.s.

Presentation of Robert de Eversdon, chaplain, to the chapel of Brok, in the diocese of Winchester, in the king's gift by reason of the lands of Nicholas de Glaumorgan, an idiot, being in his hands. By letter of the seal called the ' griffoun.' Grant for life to the king's clerk Henry de Ingelby of the keeping of the House of Converts, London, with all things pertaining to that keeping; he taking therein such fee as John de Sancto Paulo and other keepers have been accustomed to take by reason of the keeping. By p.s.

Commission to William de Gategang, king's clerk, to take into the king's hands the House of Converts, London, and induct Henry de Ingelby, king's clerk, to whom the king by letters patent has granted the keeping thereof, into corporal possession of the same.

Presentation of John Cloyer, chaplain of the chantry in the church of Westminster, s t . Olave in Old Jewry, London, to the church of St. Nicholas, Hertford, in the diocese of Lincoln, in the king's gift by reason of the priory of Bee Hellouin being in his hands as above; on an exchange of benefices with Robert de Coventre.  1353. Oct. 16. Westminster. Oct. 23. Westminster. Oct. 22. Westminster, Oct. 9. Westminster. Nov. 16. Westminster Membrane 3—cont.

Whereas Stephen Coquirel, the king's enemy and rebel, who was an adherent of his enemies of Normandy during the war between the king and his adversaries of France, holds de facto the church of St. Peter Port, Gemeseye, and collects the fruits and profits of the same to his own uses,  Nov. 20. Westminster. Nov. 3. Westminster. Dec. 16. Westminster. 1354. Jan. 16. Westminster. Membrane 5—cont. to the king's contempt and prejudice, the king has appointed the king's clerk John de Heselshawe as keeper of the said church and collector of the fruits and profits thereof during the war, that the goods thereof be not dissipated idly by his enemy, or the cure of souls there neglected, to find the charges incumbent on the church out of such fruits and profits, and to convert to his own use any surplus without rendering anything for the same; and he commands the keeper of the islands of Gerneseye, Jereseye, Serk and Aureneye, and the bailiff, jurats and others of the island of Gerneseye to permit the said John to have the keeping and collect the fruits and profits. - By K.

Remission to the prior and convert of Wenlok, for the relief of that Westminster, priory, now in the king's hands on account of the war with France, which in these days is much depressed by various adversities, of 200 marks for two years, to wit for the present year and the year fol­ lowing, out of that yearly farm of 200 marks, which they are held to render at the exchequer for the keeping of their priory. By K. on the information of the treasurer. March 17.

Grant in fee to the king's yeoman Peter le Fitheler of a messuage Westminster, in Cantebrigge, lately held by Matthew de Cantebrigge by grant for ten years of the king, which is in the king's hands as his escheat b y a felony which Boniface the Jew did. By p.s. May 7.

Commission to Geoffrey Lucy and John Elys reciting that on Westminster, behalf of the commonalty of the counties of Bedford and Buckingham it has been intimated to the king that the sheriffs of those counties for the past ten years have made divers purveyances for the king's horses there and taken many victuals to the king's use of the men of the counties, by pretext of mandates from him, for which purveyances and victuals they have paid nothing to the men of whom they were taken, although they themselves had full allowance thereof in their accounts at the exchequer, but convert the money allowed for these to their own use, and that the sheriffs, who were the king's approvers (appruiatores) there, levied divers rents and other profits pertaining to the king and did not answer for these at the exchequer; and appointing them to make inqui­ sitions and certify the king as to the whole truth of the matter. By C. MEMBRANE 13rf. Nov. 13.

Inspeximus of (1) a charter of Geoffrey de Maundevill, son and Westminster, heir of Robert de Maundevill, granting to John Gervasii de Brideport, for his homage and service, the manor of Cydyok, except the land  lying to the north of that stream which is called Wynreford, absolutely, to hold to him and his heirs, to grant, sell, bequeath or assign to whomsoever he will, except religious houses and the Jewry, rendering yearly to the grantor and his heirs in their court of Cydyok called La Coppedehull 201. a year, for all services, aids, quarrels, exactions, suits of shires, hundreds and courts, and all other secular demands pertaining to the grantor and his heirs as well as the king : saving to the grantor and his heirs wards and reliefs and free coursing of deer (bestiarum) started in his chace of Merswode. In return for which grant John gave him 500 marks in recognition. Witnesses: William Everard, then sheriff of Dorset and Somerset [1258], Eudo de Rocheford, WiUiam de Leye, John de Strode, Richard L'umene, John Cedendon, knights, Reynold de Remmesbirfy], Richard de la Chapele, James de Ludeton, Gilbert de Castello, John de Turr[i], Gilbert de Oskereswill, Walter de Madreston, John Clench, Stephen Rose and others. (2) A Release by the said Geoffrey to the said John his boys and heirs begotten of the flesh, of wards, marriages and reliefs which he could require ut in molendinis de Bride-part et manerii de Gydyok. In return for which release John granted him 50 marks. Witnesses as above, with Stephen Arwell. And con­ firmation of these to John de Chidiok, who has inherited the said manor. For I mark paid in the hanaper. Oct. 18.

Whereas Edward I by letters patent granted to the abbot and Westminster, convent of St. James's without Norhampton the house which was the school of the Jews of Norhampton with the houses before the entry of the school and the houses late of Sarah de London, a Jewess, adjoining the school, to hold of the king in mortmain, rendering to him yearly Id. b y the hands of the bailiffs of the said town, and whereas one Ralph, afterwards abbot of the same place, alienated the premises to one Martin de Mountorio and his heirs, they rendering yearly to the abbot 10«. and Martin bequeathed the same to Isabel, his daughter, and her heirs, and the said Isabel granted the same to Isabel her daughter, now the wife of Onorius Sauce, for her life, with remainder to John brother of the said Isabel son of Isabel and his heirs, the present abbot of the place has made petition to the king that, whereas the tenements have been taken into the king's hand, because the alienations aforesaid were made without the king's licence, and are now so ruinous that they d o not exceed the value of 10«. yearly, which the abbot and convent used to take out of them, and the said Onorius and Isabel are willing to surrender them and John is willing to release his right therein to them, the king will pardon the trespasses done by these alienations, and grant licence for the said Onorius and Isabel and John to surrender and quit-claim as they propose, and for the abbot and convent when again in seisin of the tenements to lease them to certain tenants in fee or for term of life, as shall seem expedient, and the king, for f mark paid by the abbot, has granted Ms petition. And the J mark has been paid in the hanaper. MEMBRANE 8. May II.

Pardon, for 201. paid to the king by Robert de la Vale, ' chivaler,* Westminster, to the said Robert for acquiring in fee from his father Robert de la Vale the manor of Neusum, held in chief, and entering therein without the king's licence : and restitution of the manor to him. May 20. On the petition of Richard de Sulby of Norhampton that, whereas Westminster. Henry HI, by charter granted to his Serjeant Richard de Exmufch an estate in fee in that house in Norhampton in a street called Cornechepynge which escheated to the said king after the death of Cok aon of Aaron, Jew of London, rendering therefor yearly to the provostahip of the said town Sd. for all service, and the said Richard afterward* granted the same to Walter Cardoun and Ellen, his wife, wad Ellen, who survived Walter, granted it to Peter son of Thomas de Leyoestre, and Peter granted it to his daughter Isabel, and Isabel alienated the same to Nicholas son of William le Sotel of Northampton, and Nicholas bequeathed it in his will to Agatha la Spicer and she gave it to petitioner who afterwards took her to wife, to hold to Mm mad his heirs, and because the said Waiter and the others after him his wife, in Culgaith, and the escheator has certified that because he found by inquisition that Margaret late the wife of Hugh de Moriceby, who held in chief, the king's widow, married Matthew de Redman without his licence and that Matthew and Margaret held as her dower a third part of the manor of Culgaith, he took that third part into the king's hand, the king, for 10 marks paid by Matthew and Margaret, has pardoned them the trespass. By K. And the 10 marks have been paid in the hanaper.  1359. Membrane 2—cont. entered into the house without the king's licence, the house has been taken into the king's hand by William Fililod, escheator in the county of Northampton, the king will pardon the trespasses and restore the house to him and Agatha, the king, for 6s. 8d. paid by Richard, has granted his petition. And the 6s. Sd. have been paid in the hanaper. May 18.

Inspeximus and confirmation of letters patent of Ralph, bishop of Westminster. Bath and Wells, dated at W Tynchescombe, on 17 June, 1361, reciting that at the supplication of Master John de Carleton, dean of the church of Wells, shewing that the habitation wherein Nicholas de Colshulle, canon of the said church, dwelt while he lived, opposite the bishop's church, by the negligence of the said Nicholas and others inhabiting it after him, against whom there is no redress (recursus), is become a total ruin that cannot be repaired, and that such habitation adjoins the dean's inn; and praying him to confer the said place on him for the enlargement of the dean's habitation, he grants the same to him in mortmain, for him to convert it into a garden (ortum) or area and throw down and dispose as he will of the houses on it. By p.s. Dec. 14.

Pardon to the prioress and nuns of Stratford atte Boghe of 41.10». 4<J. Westminster, required of them for the king's use by summons of the exchequer out of lands at Le Stewes, co. Surrey, which John de Saneto Paulo, late keeper of the House of Converts, London, granted to them to find some works of piety. By JL. E n Oct. 22.

Commission to Henry Clere, the younger, William Mat . . . and John Westminster, atte Halle, pursuant to an order made with the assent of the council, to make dihgent scrutiny in the town and port of Emnesworth, and in the adjacent arms and coasts of the sea, that none take out of the realm, without licence, gold or silver, in mass or in money, or jewels or letters of exchange, saving known merchants who have given security before the bailiffs or keepers of the ports that they will not convert the same to other uses than for the exercise of their merchandise on pain of forfeiture thereof ; and that no one bring into or take out of the realm, from or to the court of Rome or other parts beyond the seas, any letters patent, bulls, instruments or other matters prejudicial to the realm or the king's subjects ; and that no one going to the court of Rome or elsewhere abroad by the king's licence be allowed to leave the realm until he have given sufficient security in the chancery that he will not prosecute or procure anything to the loss or prejudice of the king or his subjects. Feb. 10.

Grant for life to John de Sancta Maria in Ispannia, a Jewish Westminster, convert, of such wages and houses for his sustenance in the Domus Conversorum, London, as other such converts have been wont to have, together with the profits of the gardens and other easements. By K.

Saundresdon, for the alienation in mortmain by them of 8 marks of  rent arising from 4 messuages and 2 shops in Oxford and the suburb thereof which they have of the gift and feoffment of William de Newenton, executor of the will of John son of Richard Cary, and John de Stilyngton and Alice, his wife, co-executrix of the said William, whereof 2 messuages are held of the king in burgage, one messuage of the warden of the Domus Conversorum, London, one messuage of the prior of St. Eredeswyde, one shop of the abbot of Osneye and the other of the heirs of Adam Feteplace, as appears by an inquisition taken by John de Evesham, escheator in the county of Oxford, to a chaplain to celebrate divine service daily at the altar of St. Mary in the church of St. Martin, Oxford, for the soul of the said John son of Richard, for the souls of his mother and father, and for the souls of Hugh Cary and all the faithful departed, so that the said chaplain may distrain for arrears of the said rent. Nov. 16.

Grant, for long service to the king and Edward, prince of Westminster. Aquitaine and Wales, to the king's clerk, Peter de Lacy, prebendary of the prebend of Swerdes in the cathedral church of Dublin, which prebend he holds by papal authority, that notwithstanding the ordinance lately made by the king and his great council that every man beneficed or possessed of lands or possessions in Ireland should come thither or send sufficient men according to the amount of his property before Easter in the king's forty-third year, except the king's officers staying with him on his service, the said Peter shall take all the fruits and profits pertaining to that prebend and all moneys arising therefrom as well for the time when he was in the service of the king and prince as when he was without such service, and that he may convert the fruits to his own use, have them taken where he will, and dispose of them for the whole time during which he shall have been out of Ireland as freely as if he had been con­ tinually resident in his said benefice. By p.s. April 20.

Commission to J. archbishop of York and the king's domestic Westminster, clerk, Richard de Ravenser, archdeacon of Lincoln, reciting that the king has learned that Adam de Lymbergh, now provost of the church of St. John, Beverley, not understanding the true significance of his title, against the approved rule of true doctrine, converts what is common property into his own property and gluts his own maw by the hunger of others, withdrawing from the canons, clerks, servants and ministers of the church the nourishment of life and applying their daily commons to his own uses, so that some of the beneficed canons, vicars, clerks and ministers are rendered by the poor life they lead less able to exercise divine service in the church; and appointing them, in consideration that the possessions, goods and rents of the provostship were so increased by the industry of the said Richard, while he was provost, that they are now more than sufficient to support the charges of old incumbent thereon and to minister daily and continuous livelihood to the beneficed canons, vicars, clerks and ministers of the church, to summon the said provost to their presence and compel him, even by the withdrawal of ecclesiastical benefices, manors, possessions and rents set aside to support these charges and by any other means, without excuse or fraud to make payment and satisfaction of the daily portion or distribution of bread, ale, flesh, fish and victuals due to the canons, & c , and, whenever he shall refuse to make such distribution, to take the said benefices into their hand and minister the same out of the fruits thereof by one of the parsons of the college of the said church, so that the said benefices shall remain with the said parson until the provost shall have found sufficient security to make the distribution himself without diminution or fraud, in the thirty-seventh year, stolen goods of John Godefrey, to wit, cloths of linen and wool, pepper, silk thread and wax, to the value of 20s. By p.s.  1371 Membrane 30—cont. July 15.

Whereas by an inquisition taken at the Guildhall in the parish of Westminster. St. Laurence, Old Jewry, London, on 25 January last before Simon Eyr, mayor and escheator of London, it was found that John Whitthorn of Dounton, chaplain, by his will on Monday after St. Barnabas the Apostle, 23 Edward III, bequeathed in mortmain without licence to certain chap­ lains, to celebrate divine service for the souls of John de Oxenford, late citizen and vintner of London, Walter Neel, Richard Godechepe, John de Gryssyngham and of the said John Whitthorn, his parents, kinsfolk and friends, in the church of St. James, Garlekhithe, London, 5 messuages in Old Jewry, London, and 8 messuages with two chambers belonging thereto in the said parish of St. James, which he acquired of the feoffment of John de Gryssyngham and Richard Godechepe, situated by the said church, to wit, in breadth between the church on the north and ' Temestrete ' on the south, and in length from ' Cordewanerstrete ' on the west to a small lane leading from ' Temestrete' to ' Kirounlane' on the east, and a messuage in the said parish of St. Laurence, which he acquired of the feoffment of Roger de Forsham; and that Gilbert atte Leye, on 12 May, 28 Edward III, bequeathed as above to the said church of St. James a mes­ suage with a garden in the parish of All Saints Stanyngcherche, Martlane, London, for the amending of ' Oxenford Chauntery ' there though such a chantry was never founded; Whereas it was found by an inquisition taken before Henry Westminster. Frowyk, late mayor and eseheator of London, on Friday, 26 October, 15 Henry VI, at the Guildhall that Walter de Norwico after 20 Edward I was seised as of fee of the advowson of the parish church of St. Stephen, Colmanstrete, London, and that the then prior of the house of St. Mary, Butteley, co. Suffolk, and the convent of that place acquired to them and their successors of Walter the said advowson without licence and in 16 Edward II appropriated the same without licence ; and that William, now prior, held the church on the day of the inquisition, and that the church has been a parish church from time immemorial and not a chapel nor annexed to another; and afterwards William, now prior, came and not ac­ knowledging anything contained in the inquisition, said that that which was supposed by the inquisition to be a parish church w ras from time immemorial a chapel annexed to the parish church of St. Olave, Old Jewry, London, and not a parish church, and that William Geyton, late prior of Butteley, on 1 August, 1322, and all his pre­ decessors had been seised of the advowson of the church of St. Olave, the said chapel being annexed thereto, and that on the said 1 August Stephen, bishop of London, after treating with his chapter and the archdeacon of London and others and with their consent, appropriated the church of St. Olave with the said chapel to the house of Butteley, to be held by the prior and convent as true rectors or parsons thereof, so that on the cession or death of John Brian, then rector or parson thereof, all the fruits of the church and chapel should be committed to the prior and convent; and thereafter John Brian died and the prior was seised thereof and died so seised, after whose death William Randeworth, late prior, held the church and chapel, and, he being so seised, Henry V by letters patent dated 17 September in his third year pardoned the said William all gifts, alienations and purchases in mortmain without licence ; and afterwards he died seised of the premises, and William, now prior, held the same until he was ex­ pelled by colour of the said inquisition and of letters patent dated 29 October, 15 Heniy VI, presenting John Arnold to the chapel by the name of the parish church of St. Stephen, Colmanstrete, London, which John was admitted by the ordinary ; and the king on 1 March last commanded the sheriffs of London to summon John Arnold to be in Chancery on 26 March following to shew cause why his letters should not be revoked, and the sheriffs returned that they sum­ moned him by Robert Falas and James Toller; on which day the prior appeared but John came not, whereby it was considered that the said letters should be revoked:—the letters are hereby revoked and the prior restored to his possession. May 13.
